ideas.title: Elliptic-Teichmuller (Voloch-Walker/Finotti) mod-4 lift as a low-degree, Frobenius-stable second-coordinate factor base on K_0
ideas.statement: K_0: y^2+xy=x^3+1 is defined over Z with CM by Z[(1+sqrt-7)/2]; it is its own canonical lift over W(F_2). The elliptic Teichmuller lift T: E(F_{2^n}) -> E(W_2(F_{2^n})) is a Frobenius-equivariant group homomorphism on odd-order points, and (Finotti) its second Witt coordinate x_1 = F(x_0,y_0) is a polynomial of BOUNDED degree (independent of n). Define base B_w = {P : x_1(T(P)) lies in an l-dim F_2-subspace V (or has ONB/mu_263 gamma-weight <= w)}. Because T commutes with Frobenius and is additive, relations P1+P2+P3=R lift to W_2 exactly, so the descended system acquires a second layer of equations (Witt carry of S_3 over Z/4) with bounded-degree membership on the second coordinate while the first coordinate x_0 is unrestricted.
ideas.mechanism: Frobenius-stable non-subspace base whose membership is a bounded-degree polynomial in the F_2-coordinates of x_0 (via F), plus the free Witt-carry equations S_3 mod 4 / 2 that hold on lifted relations. Membership is defined through the canonical lift, not a subspace of F_{2^n}, so it bypasses the 'no Frobenius-stable subspace at ord_n(2)=n-1' wall while staying algebraically low degree.
ideas.wall_bypassed: 'No subfield, no low-degree membership' (prime n: no Frobenius-stable F_2-subspace) and lever 6 (non-subspace Frobenius-stable bases).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The wall concerns subsets of F_{2^n} defined by F_2-linear conditions on x(P) closed under squaring. B_w is defined by a linear condition on x_1(T(P)); x_1 is a non-linear bounded-degree function of x_0, and Frobenius on W_2 is semilinear and commutes with T, so V can be chosen Frobenius-stable inside W_2-coordinates (e.g. the Teichmuller span of mu_263 orbits) without any subspace of F_{2^n} being Frobenius-stable. Also not GGM-simulable: T uses coordinates (representation-dependent), the case left open by the GGM-simulable closure. LEAD-EXO-padic-jet-canonical-lift is scoped to ordinary PRIME-field curves and to additive/logarithmic digit readouts; this idea uses the lift only as a coordinate for base membership, not as a log.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: If deg F = c is bounded and the Witt-carry equations reduce the solving degree of the descended system (or keep it at the subspace value) while B_w is Frobenius-stable (n-fold relation reuse and n^2 LA saving), the Koblitz Diem/Petit-type heuristic with m fixed and bounded d_F gives B ~ 2^{n/m'} and D = poly(n), so B*D^2 << N = 2^{n}/ (2n). Honest: this only helps if d_F of the combined system is bounded in n; if F has degree ~n or the carry layer does not lower d_F, it is a relabelled subspace base (constant factor).
ideas.prior_art: Voloch-Walker (elliptic Teichmuller lift, 2000); Finotti 'Degrees of the elliptic Teichmuller lift' (J. Number Theory 2002) and 'Minimal degree liftings' (bounded degree of x_1); Satoh canonical-lift point counting; Galbraith-Gebregiyorgis / Huang-Petit-Shinohara-Takagi Frobenius-invariant factor bases on subfield curves; ePrint 2026/2181 Schur-Macaulay Z/4 lift (different: lifts equations, not points). Searched: 'canonical lift Koblitz curve Galois ring point decomposition summation polynomial Teichmuller factor base' (WebSearch 2026-10-31): no source combining elliptic Teichmuller lift with factor bases.
ideas.novelty_status: novelty_unverified (one web search, no hit for the combination)

falsifier.design: python3 with GR(4,n)=Z/4[t]/(lift of ONB-II modulus). (a) For K_0 over F_{2^n}, compute T(P) for every odd-order P by P_hat = [2^n * a](any lift), a = 2^{-n} mod #E_odd (kills the kernel of reduction); record x_1 as a Boolean function of the n bits of x_0 (and y_0) and compute its algebraic degree (ANF via Moebius transform). (b) Build B_w with V = random l-dim subspace on x_1; generate the descended S_3 + Witt-carry system for 50 targets per cell and measure d_F with msolve over F_2 vs the plain subspace base of equal size; also relation yield vs random base of equal size.
falsifier.toy_params: n in {11, 13, 17, 19, 23} (exhaustive Moebius at n<=23 is 2^23 points), l=3..5, m=2,3; 50 targets/cell
falsifier.prediction_if_true: ANF degree of x_1 as function of x_0 bits is constant (<=4) across n=11..23; d_F of the combined system <= d_F of the equal-size subspace base and does not grow from n=13 to 23; yield equals random-base yield (monodromy) within 5%.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: ANF degree of x_1 grows with n (>= n/2), or the Witt-carry layer is in the ideal generated by the mod-2 system (zero rank gain) and d_F >= subspace d_F +1: base is a constant-factor relabelling; close lever-6 'canonical-lift coordinate' cell.

ideas.risk: Finotti's bounded degree is in terms of x_0 as a field element; as Boolean function of its F_2-coordinates, x^{2^k} terms are linear so degree stays bounded, but the T-map may only equal the elliptic Teichmuller lift up to the formal-group correction, which could be high degree; the carry equations may be ideal-redundant.

ideas.title: Koblitz ECDLP as an Artin-symbol problem in the ray class field of Q(sqrt-7) mod (tau^n-1): height-zero lift, field-degree wall
ideas.statement: Canonical lifts of points of E(F_{2^n}) on K_0/Q are torsion points of E[tau^n-1] (height exactly 0), defined over the ray class field K_m of Q(sqrt-7) of conductor m=(tau^n-1); Gal(K_m/Q(sqrt-7)) ~ (O/m)^*/O^* acts by the Hecke character, so R_hat = sigma_k(P_hat) and the ECDLP is the Artin-symbol problem. Claim to test: every height-compressing lift for CM curves factors through this, and the obstruction is field degree [Q(x(P_hat)):Q] ~ N/2, not height.
ideas.mechanism: Replace the parallelogram-law height wall by an exact CM statement: small (zero) heights are free, but the lifted points live in an extension of degree ~|E|; index calculus on Frobenius elements of small primes q of O (acting as pi_q mod m) is the endomorphism action, i.e. generic.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Heights wall (ĥ parallelogram law) and atlas lever 11 / LEAD-TRF-cm-canonical-lift-heights.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The heights wall assumes lifted points of positive height; here heights are 0 so it says nothing. LEAD-TRF-cm-canonical-lift-heights is scoped to prime-field ordinary curves with large |D| (class polynomial cost); for K_0, D=-7, h=1, the lift is free, which is exactly its 'not excluded' clause.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: None expected: Artin action by small-norm ideals = multiplication by pi_q in Z[tau], GGM-simulable; B*D^2 >= N unless a sub-|E| description of K_m (e.g. via elliptic units / Siegel units generating K_m with o(N) data) yields Frobenius identification without enumerating the orbit. Classified theory: closes lever 11 for CM Koblitz curves with an exact field-degree obstruction.
ideas.prior_art: Classical CM theory (Shimura, Deuring); Couveignes-Lercier elliptic periods; atlas LEAD-TRF-cm-canonical-lift-heights; rejected corpus IDEA-018 (ray-class descent), IDEA-211 (Coleman elliptic units). New relative to corpus: explicit height-zero/field-degree trade statement for K_0 and the falsifier below.

falsifier.design: PARI gp: for K_0 over F_{2^n}, n in {5,7,9,11,13}, compute N=#E(F_{2^n}) odd part, the ideal m=(tau^n-1) in O=Z[(1+sqrt-7)/2], bnrinit(bnfinit(x^2+7), m) ray class group order; compute the degree of the minimal polynomial over Q(sqrt-7) of x(P_hat) for a generator P_hat of E[m] via the (tau^n-1)-division polynomial factor (polresultant/factor over nf at n<=9). Check (i) |Cl_m| = phi(m)/|O^*| equals orbit size, (ii) Frobenius of small primes q (N(q)<=50) acts on reduced torsion as pi_q mod m.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: [Q(sqrt-7)(x(P_hat)):Q(sqrt-7)] = (N_odd-1)/2 exactly at every n; Frobenius identity holds 100%: lever 11 closed for CM-Koblitz with obstruction = field degree.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: some x(P_hat) has degree o(N) (e.g. a subfield of K_m fixing the orbit coordinate), which would be a genuine compressed lift and reopen lever 11 with a concrete construction.

ideas.title: Hecke-correspondence branch-selection transfers on X_0(l): extend transport conservation to selected-branch non-homomorphic maps
ideas.statement: The Hecke correspondence T_l sends P to the l+1 images phi_i(P) on l-isogenous curves; summed it is a homomorphism (conservation applies), but a deterministic branch-selection rule s(P) = phi_{i(P)}(P), i(P) chosen by a coordinate rule (min x of image), is non-homomorphic and not covered by the transport-conservation lemma. Hypothesis: decomposition counts through selected-branch transfers equal random-base counts (no gain).
ideas.mechanism: Non-homomorphic transfer built from modular-curve correspondences; the only cell of transport conservation left open.
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: The lemma needs phi to be a group homomorphism; s is piecewise-homomorphic with coordinate-dependent pieces.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: Would need the selection to correlate sums (a non-group filter) with growing gain; expected constant. Classified accounting: turns the open scope note into a measured closure.
ideas.prior_art: Transport conservation (programme); corpus ECDLP-IDEA-003 (partial scalar-power correspondence, different: target-dependent), KN-OPEN-ed922d. Hecke operators on E(F_q): classical.

falsifier.design: gp: prime p~2^14..2^18, E of prime order with l=3,5 having l+1 rational l-isogenies over F_p (Atkin primes, full splitting); base F = {P: x(P)<B}; selected-branch image base s(F) on product of target curves: count targets R in each destination whose 2-decompositions over the pushed base exist, versus random base of equal size; 20 curves.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: (idea right) coverage/yield ratio vs random base > 1.2 and growing with p.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: ratio 1.00 +- 0.03 at all p: selected-branch transfers closed as accounting.

ideas.title: Bilinear elliptic character-sum bound (Ahmadi-Shparlinski-Voloch type) as a proof that degree-d x-functional filters have O(1) gain
ideas.statement: For A,B subsets of E(F_p) and an additive character psi composed with a degree-d rational function f, |sum_{P in A,Q in B} psi(f(x(P+Q)))| <= C d sqrt(|A||B|) p^{1/2}... ; plug into the bucket-gain functional of KN-OPEN-91d4f6 to show single-bucket gain <= 1 + O(d p^{1/2}/sqrt(|A||B|)), i.e. o(1) once |A||B| >> d^2 p.
ideas.mechanism: Bilinear Weil/Bombieri bound on the elliptic addition graph; supplies the 'bilinear bound of quality theta' THM_INCBARRIER2 Theorem F asks for in the polynomial-filter case.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Wagner/k-list wall open cell KN-OPEN-91d4f6 (x-functional filters).
ideas.why_wall_hypotheses_fail: N/A: this is a closure attempt for the open cell, not a bypass.
ideas.nongenericity_argument: None; theory item closing polynomial-degree filters with d << sqrt(B). Leaves filters of degree >= sqrt(|A||B|/p) and non-polynomial (e.g. digit) filters open.
ideas.prior_art: Ahmadi-Shparlinski-Voloch 'Multiplicative order of Gauss periods / bilinear sums over elliptic curves'; Shparlinski surveys on character sums over EC; Kopparty-Kothary-Shankar 2026-10-24 (polynomial approximation of DL); programme THM_INCBARRIER2.

falsifier.design: numpy: p ~ 2^20..2^24, |A|=|B|=p^{0.55}, A,B = interval bases x<B and random; f in degree-1..6 polys (random and optimised by hill-climb over coefficients for max bucket excess); compute normalised bilinear sum and bucket excess for the event f(x(P+Q)) in [0,p/K), K=2^8.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: max normalised excess <= 3 d p^{1/2}/sqrt(|A||B|) for all tried f; gain -> 1 with p.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: an f with excess exceeding the bound by >10x that persists as p grows: the bound route fails and a structured polynomial filter exists (would be the first non-group filter).

ideas.title: Drinfeld linearity defect: measure the minimal F_2-linear (additive-polynomial) approximation of tau-adic scalar action on x-coordinates of K_0
ideas.statement: Drinfeld DLP dies because phi_a is an F_q-linear map of G_a (Scanlon). The EC analogue would be an additive polynomial L of 2-degree k with x([alpha]P) ~ L(x(P)) on a positive-density set. Hypothesis (closure): for alpha in Z[tau] not a power of tau, the best k-additive approximation agrees on at most (2^k+deg)/2^n fraction (Weil-type), so the Drinfeld mechanism has no EC analogue except Frobenius itself.
ideas.mechanism: Quantifies the structural difference asked in lever 14 as a linearity-defect number.
ideas.wall_bypassed: Lever 14 (Drinfeld analogy), currently a literature note only.
ideas.prior_art: Scanlon 2001 (J. Cryptology 14); Joux-Narayanan 2019/1329; Kopparty-Kothary-Shankar 2026 for the polynomial-approximation template.

falsifier.design: python3: K_0 over F_{2^n}; for alpha in {1+tau, 2, 1-tau, tau^2+1}, solve for additive L of 2-degree k (k+1 unknown coefficients in F_{2^n}) maximizing agreement x([alpha]P)=L(x(P)) via random sub-sampling of k+1 points + count (RANSAC); compare with random-function baseline.
falsifier.prediction_if_true: (closure holds) max agreement <= (k+3)/2^n * |E| + baseline, i.e. a handful of points.
falsifier.prediction_if_false: agreement on a constant fraction for some alpha,k: an F_2-linear structure of the scalar action, a Drinfeld-type linearisation (would reopen lever 14).
